title: Escape from the Giant Pigeon
summary: Build a complete Scratch chase game, from the first reset to the last awkward collision test.

seo.title: Escape from the Giant Pigeon | School of Code
seo.description: Build Escape from the Giant Pigeon in Scratch using coordinates, collision rules, game state, complete resets, and deliberate testing.

image.alt: Paper-textured chase stage with a start corner and striped shelter

finished_summary: Guide the Player from the lower-left corner to the striped Safe Zone while an oversized pigeon closes in. The arrow keys change x and y, Game State keeps the two endings from colliding, and R runs the same complete reset as the green flag.
game_controls: Arrow keys — move the Player on the x and y axes
Green flag — stop the old run and start from known state
R key — reset positions, variables, costumes, timer, and messages

system_flow: READY restores every actor, then leaves the stage visible for one second.
PLAYING turns on movement, pursuit, the timer, Panic, and collision checks.
Pigeon contact has priority and changes Game State to CAUGHT.
Safe Zone contact changes Game State to SAFE only when the Player is not touching the pigeon.
R and the green flag both run the same reset and return the project to READY.
teacher_checkpoints: After reset, ask the student to name every value and visual detail restored by Reset Game.
After movement, ask which keys change x and which change y. Then test all four edges.
After pursuit, confirm that the pigeon begins far away and stays still during READY.
After collision, arrange a possible double contact and confirm that CAUGHT has priority.
Before the demonstration, test a green-flag start, SAFE → R, CAUGHT → R, and three quick green-flag restarts.
test_checklist: Click the green flag three times; each run starts at the same positions with READY before PLAYING.
Win, press R, and confirm positions, variables, timer, costumes, visibility, and speech reset.
Get caught, press R, and confirm the Player returns to the normal costume.
Hold each arrow key at every stage edge; the Player remains between x -218/218 and y -158/158.
Confirm the pigeon starts at x 155, y 100 while the Player starts at x -190, y -110.
Enter the Safe Zone without pigeon contact; the state becomes SAFE exactly once.
Force an overlap near the Safe Zone; pigeon contact produces CAUGHT, never both endings.
Change each visible variable, restart, and confirm Game State, Panic, Survival Time, and Pigeon Speed reset.
Hide or change a sprite costume in the editor, then restart; every actor becomes visible in its initial costume.

debugging_guide.clue: Check all four boundary comparisons. The x rules must set x, and the y rules must set y.

debugging_guide.symptom: The pigeon catches the Player immediately
debugging_guide.clue: Check both reset positions, then confirm that pursuit runs only while Game State equals PLAYING.

debugging_guide.symptom: SAFE and CAUGHT seem to happen together
debugging_guide.clue: Keep the Safe Zone check inside the not-touching-pigeon condition. Set Game State before broadcasting the ending.

debugging_guide.symptom: R leaves an old message or costume
debugging_guide.clue: Check every Reset Actors receiver. It must restore costume, visibility, speech, and position.

debugging_guide.symptom: Panic rises in the wrong direction
debugging_guide.clue: The formula subtracts scaled distance from 100. Two later checks keep the result between 0 and 100.

builder_challenge: Change Pigeon Speed to 3 and test three routes. Adjust one starting coordinate until a careful player can still win.
inventor_challenge: Add sandwich crumbs that reduce Panic without changing Game State. Explain how each crumb can trigger only once.
boss_level_challenge: Create a second original backdrop with a new Safe Zone. Reset the stage number, actor positions, and collision rules without copying the whole game.
provisional_note: The project uses original, editable sketch-style artwork. It can be redrawn later without changing sprite names, costume centres, scripts, or downloads.

code_sections.title: Reset the game
code_sections.does: Gives every run the same starting state.
code_sections.logic: The flag broadcasts Reset Game. Its receiver sets READY, restores the variables and timer, waits for each actor to reset, then switches to PLAYING after a one-second pause.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON green flag:
    ask the whole project to reset
ON Reset Game:
    set READY and restore every value
    reset every actor
    wait for a fair start
    set PLAYING
code_sections.test: Click the green flag after a win, after a loss, and during play. Check that the same positions and values return each time.
code_sections.mistake: Setting PLAYING before the sprites move back lets the collision scripts read old positions.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Why does Reset Actors use broadcast and wait rather than an ordinary broadcast?

code_sections.title: Move the player
code_sections.does: Reads the arrow keys and changes x or y.
code_sections.logic: Movement runs only during PLAYING. Right and left change x; up and down change y. Because each key has its own check, holding two keys moves the Player diagonally.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE the game is playing:
    read the arrow keys
    change x for left or right
    change y for up or down
code_sections.test: Hold each key separately, then hold two together. Watch which coordinate changes.
code_sections.mistake: Using change y for left/right or reversing the negative signs.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask the student to predict the new coordinate before pressing each arrow once.

code_sections.title: Keep the player on stage
code_sections.does: Keeps the whole Player visible inside the stage.
code_sections.logic: Four comparisons watch the current x and y positions. When the Player passes a limit, the script puts the matching coordinate back on the edge.
code_sections.pseudocode:
FOREVER during PLAYING:
    if x passes either side, put x on the edge
    if y passes top or bottom, put y on the edge
code_sections.test: Hold every arrow key against every boundary, including two diagonal corners.
code_sections.mistake: Checking an x boundary and accidentally setting y.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Why are the limits smaller than the stage edges at x -240/240 and y -180/180?

code_sections.title: Start the pigeon
code_sections.does: Returns the pigeon to its known starting position and appearance.
code_sections.logic: Reset Actors restores the pigeon's position, direction, costume, and visibility. The Stage stays in READY for one second, so the pigeon cannot begin chasing early.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON Reset Actors:
    stop any old chase appearance
    move far from the Player
    face left, show wings up, and show
code_sections.test: Move the pigeon and change its costume during a run. Restart and check that every starting property returns.
code_sections.mistake: Resetting only the position while an ending costume or hidden state remains.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Before PLAYING begins, compare the two starting positions and explain why the distance is fair.

code_sections.title: Chase the player
code_sections.does: Points towards the Player and moves by Pigeon Speed.
code_sections.logic: The loop aims again after every move because the Player's position keeps changing. A short wait controls the chase speed and leaves enough time to see the wing costumes alternate.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE the game is PLAYING:
    point toward the Player's current position
    move by Pigeon Speed
    flap once and pause briefly
code_sections.test: Move in a large rectangle and confirm the pigeon continually corrects its direction.
code_sections.mistake: Pointing toward the Player once before the loop instead of during every chase step.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Which variable changes the difficulty without changing the chase script?

code_sections.title: Detect being caught
code_sections.does: Sets CAUGHT once when the Player touches the pigeon.
code_sections.logic: The outer Game State check prevents a repeated ending. The script sets CAUGHT before broadcasting, so every other PLAYING system stops at its next check.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE PLAYING:
    if touching the Giant Pigeon:
        set CAUGHT first
        announce Caught
code_sections.test: Let the pigeon touch the Player from several directions and confirm CAUGHT appears once.
code_sections.mistake: Broadcasting the ending before changing state allows another detector to run as if play continues.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: On the contact frame, which command prevents the second ending from running?

code_sections.title: Detect reaching safety
code_sections.does: Sets SAFE only when the Player reaches the shelter without touching the pigeon.
code_sections.logic: The outer not-touching-pigeon check gives CAUGHT priority when both contacts appear to happen together. Only after that check does the script test the Safe Zone.
code_sections.test: Reach the shelter cleanly, then drag the pigeon over it and test the overlap priority.
code_sections.mistake: Testing safety without excluding pigeon contact makes the ending depend on script timing.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask the student to explain why the Safe Zone condition sits inside the pigeon condition.

code_sections.title: Update the panic meter
code_sections.does: Calculates Panic from distance and records survival time.
code_sections.logic: Panic rises as the pigeon gets closer. Two checks keep it between 0 and 100. A separate Stage script records the timer to the nearest tenth while the game is PLAYING.
code_sections.pseudocode:
WHILE PLAYING:
    Panic = 100 - rounded(distance / 4)
    clamp Panic between 0 and 100
    Survival Time = timer rounded to tenths
code_sections.test: Watch Panic at the starting distance, during the chase, and on contact. Restart and check that Panic and Survival Time return to zero.
code_sections.mistake: Dividing 100 by distance instead of subtracting scaled distance makes the meter jump unpredictably.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Why can Panic be approximate while the ending still uses direct touching?

code_sections.title: End the game cleanly
code_sections.does: Shows the result with a costume, sound, message, and Safe Zone change.
code_sections.logic: The detector commits the Game State before the ending receivers change the presentation. Movement and pursuit stop because their scripts only run during PLAYING.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON Caught:
    show caught costume and sound
    explain how to restart
ON Reached Safety:
    activate the shelter and play its sound
    explain how to restart
code_sections.test: Trigger each ending and check that no sound, costume, message, or state from the other ending appears.
code_sections.mistake: Using stop all before displaying the result prevents ending feedback and restart scripts.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Which scripts stop because Game State changed, even though they contain no stop block?

code_sections.title: Restart and test
code_sections.does: Sends the R key and green flag through the same reset.
code_sections.logic: There is one Reset Game receiver, so a repair applies to both ways of restarting. R works after a win, after a loss, and during play.
code_sections.pseudocode:
ON R key:
    ask for Reset Game and wait
THEN test green flag, win-restart, caught-restart, edges, overlap, and variables
code_sections.test: Run the full checklist, including three flag clicks and an R restart after each ending.
code_sections.mistake: Copying the reset commands under R gives the project two reset scripts that can drift apart.
code_sections.teacher_checkpoint: Ask the student to demonstrate one repaired bug and the test that would catch it again.

scripts.source:
when green flag clicked
broadcast [Reset Game v] and wait

when [r v] key pressed
broadcast [Reset Game v] and wait

when I receive [Reset Game v]
set [Game State v] to [READY]
stop all sounds
set [Panic v] to (0)
set [Survival Time v] to (0)
set [Pigeon Speed v] to (2)
reset timer
broadcast [Reset Actors v] and wait
wait (1) seconds
set [Game State v] to [PLAYING]
play sound [start v] until done

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        set [Survival Time v] to ((round ((timer) * (10))) / (10))
    end
end

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
set rotation style [left-right v]
go to x: (-190) y: (-110)
switch costume to [normal v]
show
say []

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <key [right arrow v] pressed?> then
            change x by (5)
        end
        if <key [left arrow v] pressed?> then
            change x by (-5)
        end
        if <key [up arrow v] pressed?> then
            change y by (5)
        end
        if <key [down arrow v] pressed?> then
            change y by (-5)
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <(x position) > (218)> then
            set x to (218)
        end
        if <(x position) < (-218)> then
            set x to (-218)
        end
        if <(y position) > (158)> then
            set y to (158)
        end
        if <(y position) < (-158)> then
            set y to (-158)
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <touching [Giant Pigeon v]?> then
            set [Game State v] to [CAUGHT]
            broadcast [Caught v]
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        if <not <touching [Giant Pigeon v]?>> then
            if <touching [Safe Zone v]?> then
                set [Game State v] to [SAFE]
                broadcast [Reached Safety v]
            end
        end
    end
end

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        set [Panic v] to ((100) - (round ((distance to [Giant Pigeon v]) / (4))))
        if <(Panic) < (0)> then
            set [Panic v] to (0)
        end
        if <(Panic) > (100)> then
            set [Panic v] to (100)
        end
    end
end

when I receive [Caught v]
switch costume to [caught v]
play sound [caught v] until done
say [CAUGHT! Press R to restart.]

when I receive [Reached Safety v]
say [SAFE! Press R to restart.]

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
set rotation style [all around v]
go to x: (155) y: (100)
point in direction (-90)
switch costume to [wings up v]
show

when green flag clicked
forever
    if <(Game State) = [PLAYING]> then
        point towards [Player v]
        move (Pigeon Speed) steps
        next costume
        wait (0.08) seconds
    end
end

when I receive [Reset Actors v]
go to x: (190) y: (-115)
switch costume to [inactive v]
show

when I receive [Reached Safety v]
switch costume to [active v]
play sound [safe v] until done
